newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz sees short-term election "noise".
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz sees short-term election "noise".

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said in an interview published Tuesday that upcoming mid-term elections would cause "short-term noise," but added the democratic opening is good for the economy.

Ortiz told the daily El Financiero that July 6 elections for the whole of Congress, one quarter of the Senate, six governorships and the mayor of Mexico City, could generate some instability in markets.
But he said the markets may also be soothed by progress in Mexico's democratic opening.
"For me, it could result in the reverse happening. I think that the political rivalry that we are living through is something very sane," he said.
"Political opening and political rivalry is good for the economy, it is not bad, although it could provoke a little bit of short-term noise," Ortiz said.

"Investors inside and outside (the country) are going to be much more confident in investing in a country with a solid electoral institution," he added, refering to the Federal Electoral Institute which was reformed last year with independent counsellors appointed.

"When political parties start to unveil their economic plans, announcing work programs, they are trying to get closer to the electorate with solid proposals and a sound electoral debate moves forward," he added.
